source.reason: Discussion of the shear strengthening mechanism that governs the κ-carbide contribution in these solution-treated low-density steels, including the 20%Mn composition.

interaction_type.value: particle shear (dislocation glide across κ-carbide shear planes)

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Strengthening contribution of the κ-carbides is described by a particle shear model (σ_shear = α f^1/2 d_Car^1/2) rather than an Orowan mechanism; shear deformation also facilitates the glide of dislocations across κ-carbide shear planes, resulting in weakened work hardening. The paper's fit gives a slope of 97.1 MPa/nm^1/2 for yield strength versus d_Car^0.5 and states shear strengthening is still active for κ-carbide sizes as large as 50 nm.

slip_behavior.value: The κ-carbides are sheared by gliding dislocations (particle shear model) rather than bypassed by Orowan looping; this shear deformation lowers the work hardening rate as the κ-carbide size increases. The 20%Mn steel has the largest κ-carbides (18 nm) of the Mn series and correspondingly the lowest work hardening rate of that series.

phase_evolution.value: κ-carbides precipitate from spinodal decomposition and ordering of C and Al in the austenite phase during the 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment; their size in the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series decreases with increasing Mn content (18 nm at 20%Mn, 5 nm at 25%Mn, 3 nm at 30%Mn, 2 nm at 35%Mn).

interface_notes.value: Small amounts of ferrite (3.30 vol% in the 20%Mn steel) are present in addition to the austenite/K-carbide interfaces; the austenite grain size is refined by the ferrite phase. No intergranular κ-carbides are reported for this sample.
